Om stillingen

Som Market Access Coordinator hos Danske Commodities bliver du en central del af vores Market Access-team, der arbejder med at sikre, at vores produkter og løsninger overholder de gældende regler og standarder på de markeder, vi opererer på. Du vil indgå i et tværfagligt team, hvor du samarbejder tæt med kolleger inden for supply chain, compliance, sales og produktudvikling. Rollen er en midlertidig stilling som barselsvikar, og du vil få ansvaret for at sikre kontinuitet i vores market access-arbejde i en periode.

**Stay ahead of real-world threats — protecting what connects Denmark

**Join a mission that matters. As Denmark’s digital backbone, TDC NET powers millions of connections every day. We're hiring an experienced penetration tester to find and expose vulnerabilities before malicious actors do.

About the job

As TDC NET’s new Penetration Tester, your primary mission is to improve the security of Denmark’s critical digital infrastructure through adversarial testing across a broad range of technologies.

Your work will span multiple technical domains, including complex web applications, Active Directory environments, hardware and CPE security, mobile networks, AI systems, and cloud infrastructure. You will collaborate with engineers, platform owners, and security stakeholders to translate findings into lasting security improvements.

Beyond delivery, you will also contribute to the team’s culture and external engagement through research and community activities—such as helping organize the yearly TDC NET CTF for the Danish community, participating in conferences and training events.

More than just finding vulnerabilities, you'll guide teams through attacker thinking, help them prioritize what matters most, and play a key role in raising TDC NET's overall security maturity.

Key Responsibilities

• Plan and execute penetration tests and adversary-emulation activities

• Identify vulnerabilities and misconfigurations

• Deliver clear, actionable penetration testing reports

• Contribute to research, internal tooling and knowledge sharing, and community engagement

About the team

You will be joining a focused team of 4 full-time penetration testers—specialists who work side by side, learn from each other, and take on security challenges spanning a broad range of systems, platforms, and technologies.

Our culture is built on trust, inclusion, and open dialogue—where we encourage one another to grow and create impact that is greater than the sum of our individual contributions.

“Pentesting here isn’t about ticking boxes — it’s about staying one step ahead of real adversaries. You’ll work with curious, skilled people who challenge assumptions, sharpen each other’s craft, and test systems that truly matter for the Danish society,” says Cristiano Iria

About you

Your mindset is key - We’re looking for someone who is:

• Curious and courageous in daily work, motivated to explore new approaches and pursue novel ideas

• Energized by change and continuous learning

• At home with extended screen time and genuinely interested in diving into technical rabbit holes.

• Inspired by the mission to safeguard Denmark’s critical infrastructure and national resilience

• A skilled communicator and collaborator, able to build trust across teams

Whether you're early in your career or a skilled specialist, we encourage you to apply - we value potential and passion as much as experience.

Experience & Skills

• Extensive experience in penetration testing experience in complex environments (e.g., consulting, internal red team, offensive security role or well-rounded CTF background)

• Proficiency in several of the following areas:

• Web application and API security testing

• Active Directory and Entra ID security assessments

• Network and service testing within complex infrastructures

• Experience with hardware, CPE, or embedded security testing (interfaces, firmware, device exposure)

• Background in telco or critical infrastructure security

• Ability to produce high-quality reports and communicate findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences

• Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance from Danish authorities. Eligibility for security clearance requires EU citizenship or residence in the EU for at least seven years.

jobs.description:
We are offering a position as clinical assistant in brain tumor research commencing 1 January 2027.

Our group and research

The selected candidate will be part of professor, consultant neuropathologist Bjarne Winther Kristensens research group. Bjarne Winther Kristensen will be the supervisor. The research group focus on glioblastoma, the most frequent and malignant type of brain cancer. Patients diagnosed with glioblastomas are among those cancer patients that have the poorest overall survival. By understanding and overcoming the mechanisms of aggressiveness and resistance in glioblastoma, we strive to discover novel molecular targets for more effective therapies for the patients.

Your job

You will join a multi-disciplinary research team that work with both patient tumor tissue, experimental in vitro and in vivo brain tumor models and advanced bioinformatics using a multi-omics approach. The ideal candidate should have a strong background in pathology, including formal training in pathology and a PhD in pathology-oriented brain tumor research. The candidate should have a particular interest in investigating the spatial and temporal biology of glioblastoma, with a focus on understanding the mechanisms underlying tumor aggressiveness and progression. The successful candidate will take responsibility for managing and further developing our glioblastoma patient tissue cohort. The candidate will also be expected to co-supervise Ph.D. and Master's students and actively contribute to the scientific development of the research group. We are looking for a highly motivated, independent, and collaborative researcher with strong organizational and communication skills. The ideal candidate should be able to coordinate multiple research collaborations, take scientific initiative, and independently drive research projects forward.

Start: 1. January 2027

Duration: Permanent

Key criteria for the assessment of applicants

Applicants must hold an MD degree and have completed a Ph.D. with a thesis relevant to the research area of the project. The applicant must have submitted their PhD thesis before the application deadline.

Other important criteria are:

• Professional qualifications relevant to the project

• Previous publications

• Relevant work experience

• Experience with supervision

• Other professional activities

• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in brain tumor biology

• Language skills

Place of employment

The place of employment is the Bartholin Institute, Department og Pathology, Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet. We are also part of Biotech Research and Innovation Center (BRIC) and Department of Clinical Medicine, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and platforms for spatial analyses.

Terms of employment

• Permanent position. The position is associated with a project funded by the Danish Medical Research Council, with project-related tasks expected to extend over two years,

• The average weekly working hours are 37 hours

• Salary, pension, and terms of employment are in accordance with the Danish Regions’ guidelines and the collective agreement for junior doctors (Agreement No. 33.06.1).

Questions

For specific information about the position, please contact professor Bjarne Kristensen, email: bjarne.winther.kristensen.01@regionh.dk

General information about PhD studies at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences is available at the Graduate School’s website, se here.

Application process

Your application must be submitted electronically by clicking ‘Apply now’ before Thuesday, December 8, 2026 23.59pm CET (Copenhagen local time).

Required documents (in PDF-format)

• Motivation letter (1 - 2 pages maximum) describing your relevant expertise, research interest and career plans

• CV including education, work/research experience, language skills and other relevant qualifications

• Certified copies of:

• PhD certificate (or superviser’s statement if pending)

• Master’s degree

• Academic transcripts for relevant degrees

• Complete list of publications

• Optional: Letter(s) of recommendation

Note: Only applications submitted through the electronic system will be considered. Application received via email or other platforms will not be processed due to administrative reasons. We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

jobs.description:
Shape the future of our chip and chipset test capabilities, bringing together technology, people and priorities

About the team and the role

Chipset Test & Support is responsible for testing and validating our chips and chipsets throughout their development. Our work ranges from testing and characterization of standalone silicon to testing the complete chipset as an integrated system.

The team works across hardware and software, developing test systems, test boards, automation and software tools for efficient and reliable testing. We also deliver and support test boards used by engineering teams across the organization for chipset bring-up, development, debugging and validation.

Looking ahead, we are shaping our future test architecture, systems and automation strategy, including the software platforms needed for test of future generations of chips and chipsets.

As Product Owner, you will help shape this direction, translating current and future needs into clear priorities and a coherent roadmap. You will maintain the overview across stakeholders and chipset programs, balancing immediate delivery and support with longer-term investments.

You do not need to be the technical expert, but you should be curious about technology and motivated to develop a solid understanding of the hardware and software systems behind our test solutions, enabling you to recognize dependencies, evaluate trade-offs and make informed product decisions.

Your key responsibilities

• Maintain an overview of requirements, commitments, dependencies and risks across stakeholders and chipset programs.

• Prioritize competing needs and create clarity around trade-offs and decisions.

• Balance short-term deliveries and support with longer-term development of test systems, software, automation and architecture.

• Engage with engineering teams, partners and stakeholders to understand their needs and feedback, and turn these insights into clear priorities and plans.

• Work closely with the team, Scrum Master/Team Coach, fellow Product Owners, architects, Product Management and the Release Train Engineer to align priorities, dependencies and plans across the ART.

• Foster collaboration across teams, technical disciplines and organizational boundaries.

Qualifications

We are looking for someone who combines a strong interest in technology with excellent collaboration, communication and prioritization skills.

Ideally, you bring:

• Technical curiosity and the ability to develop sufficient understanding of complex hardware and software systems to make informed product decisions, while relying on engineers and architects for technical expertise.

• Experience coordinating complex development activities and multiple stakeholders, with the ability to establish priorities and drive decisions.

• The ability to maintain the overview and make decisions when requirements and priorities compete.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the confidence to challenge assumptions and create alignment.

• Experience or knowledge within PCB design, electronics, lab testing, test and measurement, software architecture and/or test automation is highly relevant.

• A background in electrical engineering, electronics or another relevant technical field is desirable.

• Experience working with Agile development teams is beneficial.

Success in the role

Success in the first 12–18 months would mean that you are well integrated into both the Chipset Test & Support team and the wider PO team, with strong working relationships across the ART. You will have helped bring the current test campaign to a successful completion while keeping priorities and dependencies clear. At the same time, the team will be well prepared for the next test campaign, with the necessary test systems, software and automation updated and ready to support it.

You will design and integrate digital functionality for future generations of ultra-low-power SoCs. Working in a Scrum team within our SAFe organization, you will collaborate with architects and specialists across verification, physical design, analog design, firmware and systems engineering.

• Turning system and architectural ideas into robust design concepts and microarchitectures

• Experience defining microarchitectures and implementing complex digital blocks or subsystems

You will work with experienced specialists across the complete IC lifecycle and contribute to products that help people hear, communicate and participate more fully in everyday life.
